Background CD226, an activating receptor expressed on the surface of natural killer (NK) cells and T cells, is also seen on B cells and CD226 polymorphism is associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Because the specific roles of CD226 + B cells in SLE are still unknown, we investigated the association of CD226 + B cells with SLE. Methods We measured CD226 expression on B cells and its subsets using flow cytometry in 48 SLE patients and 24 healthy controls (HCs). We assessed the relationships between CD226 + B cells and SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K), clinical manifestations, laboratory data, and prognosis after 12 months. Results The proportions of CD226 + cells in whole B cells and all its subsets were significantly higher in SLE patients than HCs. In SLE patients, the proportions of CD226 + B cells and CD226 + switched-memory (SM) B cells were significantly correlated with SLEDAI-2K scores and anti-dsDNA antibody titers, and negatively correlated with serum complement levels. Moreover, basal percentages of CD226 + B cells and CD226 + SM B cells were low in patients who were in Lupus Low Disease Activity State after 12 months. In patients with renal involvement, the proportion of CD226 + B cells increased. Additionally, the proportion of CD226 + B cells was higher in patients who were not in complete renal remission after 12 months. Conclusions Increased proportion of CD226 + B cells was associated with disease activity and prognosis of SLE. CD226 + B cells may be a useful biomarker for the management of SLE. systemic lupus erythematosus CD226 B cells lupus low disease activity lupus nephritis Japan Society for the Promotion of Science 10.13039/501100001691 Introduction Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease with various clinical manifestations and its management is often difficult ( 1 – 3 ). Recently, the concept of treat-to-target (T2T) in SLE has been established, and it has been more important to monitor disease activity and predict the prognosis of SLE ( 3 – 5 ). Because of this, many studies have tried to find potential novel biomarkers from the molecules involved in the pathogenesis of SLE ( 6 , 7 ). Although the pathogenesis of SLE is not yet fully understood, it is known that genetic factors contribute to the development of SLE ( 2 , 8 – 10 ) and that various immune cells are involved in the immune responses in SLE ( 11 ). In particular, B cells play an important role in the pathogenesis of SLE by autoantibody and cytokine production and antigen presentation ( 8 , 11 – 13 ). Some B cell phenotypes have been reported as useful biomarkers for disease activity of SLE ( 7 , 13 ); however, these have not yet been established. Several genome-wide association studies have reported the importance of the CD226 gene in the susceptibility to SLE in multiple ancestries ( 14 – 17 ). CD226 is expressed on the cell surface of T cells, natural killer (NK) cells, B cells, monocytes, and platelets ( 18 ). It also acts as an activating receptor and mediates cytotoxicity and has been reported to modulate various immune functions as well ( 18 – 21 ). Moreover, several studies have shown the involvement of CD226 in autoimmune diseases such as SLE ( 22 ), rheumatoid arthritis ( 23 ), and systemic sclerosis ( 24 ). On the other hand, the immune functions of CD226 on B cells remain unclear, although a recent study suggested CD226 was involved in adaptive immune responses of B cells ( 25 ). This study aimed to reveal the involvement of CD226 on B cells in the pathogenesis of SLE by measuring CD226 expression on B cells using flow cytometry in SLE patients and by assessing the relationship between CD226-expressing B cells and the disease activity, clinical manifestations, and prognosis of SLE.

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis, B cell immunity, and disease activity.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: CD226 is an activating/costimulatory receptor expressed on B cells (also T cells, NK cells, monocytes, platelets). It binds to CD112 and CD155, with TIGIT acting as a coinhibitory paired receptor. CD226 mediates cytotoxicity and modulates immune functions, involved in adaptive immune responses. In SLE, increased proportions of CD226+ B cells, particularly switched-memory (SM) B cells and plasmablasts, are involved in pathogenesis and correlate with disease activity. Their upregulation might be influenced by Toll-like receptor (TLR) 9 stimulation and they are implicated in IL-10 and autoantibody production, contributing to SLE outcomes and renal involvement.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: The proportion of CD226+ B cells shows a clear association with disease intensity and prognosis: it is lower in patients achieving Lupus Low Disease Activity State (LLDAS) after 12 months and those achieving complete renal remission, while it increases with renal involvement and in patients who do not achieve complete renal remission. However, no significant correlation was found with prednisolone equivalent dose (ρ = 0.09; P = 0.54) or the use of immunosuppressive agents (23.0% vs 21.4%; P = 0.76).
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: The increase in CD226+ cells is observed across all B cell subsets in SLE patients compared to healthy controls. Specifically, CD226+ B cells and CD226+ switched-memory (SM) B cells exhibit significant correlations with SLEDAI-2K scores, anti-dsDNA antibody titers, and complement levels, showing stronger associations than other B cell subsets or plasmablasts (which showed non-significant relations). The elevation of CD226+ B cells is notably specific to patients with renal, musculoskeletal, and/or hematological manifestations, particularly pronounced in renal involvement where it reflects renal disease activity. This distinguishes the findings from prior research primarily focused on CD226 expression on NK cells.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: Patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), specifically Japanese patients (N=48) from Kyushu University Hospital, including those with active disease, renal involvement (Lupus Nephritis), and other clinical manifestations such as musculoskeletal and hematological involvement. Healthy controls (N=24) were used for comparison. The study also included patients with refractory manifestations like Neuropsychiatric SLE (NPSLE).
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: An increased proportion of CD226+ B cells is associated with higher disease activity and a less favorable prognosis in SLE patients. This biomarker reflects SLE pathogenesis, disease status, and predicts long-term outcomes, including renal prognosis after 12 months. It is positively correlated with anti-dsDNA antibody titers.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: adverse risk/diagnostic utility. Higher levels of CD226+ B cells are associated with increased disease activity, poorer prognosis, and failure to achieve remission in renal lupus.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: CD226+ B cells, especially CD226+ switched-memory (SM) B cells, are suggested to reliably reflect SLE disease activity and prognosis, including long-term outcomes and renal prognosis (after 12 months). Their frequency decreased with treatment improvement and increased with disease impairment, highlighting their utility as a prognostic and monitoring marker, differentiating them from conventional biomarkers like anti-dsDNA titers and complement levels which primarily reflect disease activity but not prognosis. However, the study acknowledges that their utility, like other B cell phenotypes for SLE disease activity, has not yet been fully established and results require validation in larger, prospective, multicenter studies due to current single-center and retrospective study limitations.
